- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67) followed by a spike in forecast, reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -0.33 or lower) and forecast rises, lower forecast by 3–8% to counteract sentiment-driven overreaction.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days (e.g., 30d forecast vs 30d true), adjust model to slightly underpredict early peaks and overpredict late troughs.
- When sentiment volatility is high (e.g., >2 changes in 3 days), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±1–2% deviation from trend to capture sentiment-driven noise.
- If news volume is low (0.0) and sentiment is neutral or negative, model should not overreact — cap forecast adjustments to ±1% of recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model should anticipate a 2–4 day lag — adjust forecast to dip 1–3% below peak 2–3 days later.
